LanguageData.PWU_TraitChangeBaseComponentCost: Base component cost per trait change: {0}
LanguageData.PWU_TraitChangeBaseComponentCostDesc: Advanced components charged for every trait change that doesn't cross the base/persona boundary (both additions and removals cost, neither refunds). Charged regardless of the weapon's quality. Installing a persona core on the first trait, or refunding it on the last, is unaffected by this setting.
LanguageData.PWU_TraitChangeQualitySurchargeThreshold: The weapon quality tier at which the per-level component surcharge below starts applying. Trait changes on weapons at or below this quality cost only the base component amount.
LanguageData.PWU_TraitChangeQualitySurchargePerLevelD: Extra advanced components charged per quality tier above the surcharge threshold. For example, at the default threshold (Normal) and per-level value (1), a Masterwork weapon costs 3 more components per trait change than the base amount.
LanguageData.PWU_CostTableHeader: Advanced components required per trait change, by weapon quality:
LanguageData.PWU_WipeBondingComponentCostDesc: Advanced components charged to wipe a persona weapon's bond, returning it to bond-on-next-equip.
LanguageData.PWU_WipeKillTrackerComponentCostDesc: Advanced components charged to wipe a persona weapon's kill memory.
LanguageData.PWU_MinimumQualityDesc: Restrict customization to weapons of at least this quality. Awful imposes no restriction. Weapons below the minimum will still show the customization option, but it will be disabled with an explanation.
LanguageData.PWU_RequireCustomizationResearchDesc: Require the completion of the Bladelink Customization research project before customizing weapons. When disabled, the project is hidden from the research tree.
LanguageData.PWU_TechprintCountDesc: Number of Bladelink Customization techprints required to complete the research, on top of its research point cost. Setting this to 0 removes the techprint requirement entirely and stops traders from stocking the print. Takes effect immediately, no restart needed.
LanguageData.PWU_EnableMonoswordRecipeDesc: Show the "make monosword" bill at the fabrication bench (requires Bladelink Customization research). Disabling this only hides it from the add-bill menu; bills already queued keep producing.
LanguageData.PWU_EnablePlasmaswordRecipeDesc: Show the "make plasmasword" bill at the fabrication bench (requires Bladelink Customization research). Disabling this only hides it from the add-bill menu; bills already queued keep producing.
LanguageData.PWU_EnableZeushammerRecipeDesc: Show the "make zeushammer" bill at the fabrication bench (requires Bladelink Customization research). Disabling this only hides it from the add-bill menu; bills already queued keep producing.
LanguageData.PWU_AllowDefConversionDesc: Allow weapons to convert between base and persona defs during customization. When disabled, only already-persona weapons can be customized, and removing all traits keeps the weapon as a zero-trait persona weapon instead of reverting to its base weapon.
LanguageData.PWU_EnforceMaxTraitLimitDesc: Vanilla persona weapons generate with no more than two traits. Enable this to enforce the same limit during customization. Disable to allow any number of traits (other rules such as exclusion restrictions still apply).
LanguageData.PWU_EnforceSoleTraitDesc: Some traits cannot be the only trait on a weapon during vanilla generation. Enable this to enforce the same restriction during customization.
LanguageData.PWU_RestrictTraitsToDiscovered: Restrict available traits to discovered weapons
LanguageData.PWU_RestrictTraitsToDiscoveredDesc: A lightweight progression system: when enabled, the customization dialog only offers traits found on persona weapons the colony has seen: unfogged and unsealed on a loaded map, or carried in a player-faction caravan. Weapons carried by hostiles count too, but their traits stay disabled until the weapon is captured. No persistent state is added to saves; toggling this off restores the full trait list immediately.
LanguageData.PWU_EnableGroundCustomizationDesc: Show "Customize" options when right-clicking weapons on the ground. Disable this to reduce float menu clutter, especially with storage mods that stack items in the same cell. Weapons can still be customized by selecting them and using the gizmo button.
LanguageData.PWU_IntegrateVpweCustomizationDesc: Add a Texture tab to PWU's customization dialog for editing a Vanilla Persona Weapons Expanded weapon's composed appearance (grip, blade, and similar parts), and hide VEF's own separate "Customize" ground float-menu option wherever PWU's own customize option is available, giving you one unified place to edit a persona weapon instead of two competing menu entries. Enabled by default; disable this to keep the separate VPWE workflow untouched.
LanguageData.PWU_HaulPlannerSequentialDesc: Vanilla behavior. Pawns carry up to one ingredient stack at a time, always grabbing the nearest first. Simple and predictable, but means lots of short trips for resource-heavy customizations.
LanguageData.PWU_HaulPlannerSweepDesc: Pawns plan ahead and use spare inventory space to carry more at once, while also routing more efficiently between pickups. Far fewer trips than Sequential, with negligible planning overhead.
LanguageData.PWU_HaulPlannerThoroughDesc: Like Sweep, but also weighs which stacks to draw from when the map has multiple candidates, rather than always taking the closest. Slower to plan, but usually finds the shortest runs when ingredients are scattered or carrying capacity is tight. Falls back to Sweep for hauls too complex to fully analyze.
